concerns.message: The plan never says when a carrier-sighting rumor goes stale. The generic rule is 'stale when the target no longer holds a copy of that type'. For a sector target that is a carrier, that means staleness is checked against the carrier's current position. The victim would get a stale message on the exact tick the carrier leaves the sector, which is live information. The journal would then offer a replacement: another sector from 30 s earlier, because every copy is still carried. That replacement goes stale on the next crossing, and the cycle repeats.
concerns.consequence: Well before minute 28, a player who lost a rubbing gets a continuous sector-level tracker on the thief: a live stale signal at each crossing plus a fresh delayed sector each time. That breaks the task's 'never a free tracker' and §11's 'rather than an exact continuous tracker', and it makes the minute-28 public reveal (every 30 s) pointless. The hidden-information property test only looks for exact positions and ids, so it passes anyway. The flaw would only show up when objectives-endgame wires the module in, and fixing it then means reworking the staleness model and its tests. Before workers start, settle this: a carrier sighting is a one-shot snapshot that carrier movement never makes stale (retire it only when that copy stops being carried, or when the holder gets the type), and replacement sightings come at most once per carrier interval per player.

concerns.message: Acceptance 5 asks for property runs 'over 20,000 ticks, crossing all reveal times'. At 20 ticks/s, minute 20 is tick controlStart+24,000 and minute 28 is +33,600, so 20,000 ticks with the real constants reaches neither.
concerns.consequence: A worker who takes the numbers literally gets an EXERCISED failure for the minute-20 and minute-28 message kinds, or quietly drops them from coverage. Either the property config shortens the reveal times (still in order, so the content validator accepts them) or the runs go past about 36,000 ticks. Tell the worker which one, and keep the scripted boundary tests on the real constants.

concerns.message: Fresh rumors and route active/inactive have to come from diffing each player's held types between ticks. The ledger's `freshRumors` can't serve as the signal: it is a sticky, deduplicated flag that is never drained, so a second loss of the same type doesn't change it (duels.ts:218). Diffing only works if the world view's 'held types' includes duel-reserved rubbings, as ledger `heldTypes` does.
concerns.consequence: If the caller builds held types only from `player`-located rubbings, every duel reservation looks like losing everything. That triggers spurious fresh rumors, 'route inactive' messages and new starting-style leads, then 'restored' when the duel is cancelled. docs/intel.md and the world-view type should state that held = owned + reserved, and that a player who has left gets no loss rumors.

concerns.message: The carrier history 'keeps each carrier's sector from the last 30 s'. If it is keyed by current carriers, a thief who just stole has no sample from 30 s earlier. That is exactly §11's fresh-rumor case where every other copy is carried.
concerns.consequence: The worker ends up with an undefined sighting, a crash, or a fallback to the current sector, and the fallback breaks the 'never the current one' rule. Key the history by player (sector transitions over the last 600 ticks, bounded) so a sample from 30 s earlier always exists after the first 30 s. Also define what happens before 30 s of history exists.

concerns.message: The plan doesn't say what a minute-28 carrier broadcast or a carrier sighting contains: sector only, sector plus type, or sector plus the carrier's player id. §16 lists enemy inventories as hidden. The property test's oracle is written by the same worker who writes the messages.
concerns.consequence: Messages could name which player carries which type to everyone, and the self-written check would still pass. Pin the payload down (for example, anonymous sector and type), and make the hidden-information check structural: message types have no position or id fields except the final-island route.

concerns.message: Reveals are specified 'at exact boundary ticks', and the history assumes one call per tick. If objectives-endgame ever skips a tick or batches ticks, equality checks on the tick miss the reveal.
concerns.consequence: The minute-20 or minute-28 reveal could be silently skipped in the wired match. Trigger on the first tick at or after the boundary and keep a 'done'/'next due' record in state, so the reveal is idempotent. That costs nothing now.

concerns.message: A rumor whose type the holder has since collected or stolen falls under neither 'stale' nor 'replacement'.
concerns.consequence: A naive rule marks it stale and then offers a replacement for a type the player already holds, which breaks acceptance 2. Retire such rumors silently, and add a scripted test for it.

simpler_alternative: Split leads into two kinds. Journal rumors only ever target islands (sealed sources) or cache sectors; only these go stale and get replacements. A carrier sighting is a one-shot message with no staleness tracking. It is sent only on the three §11/§3 triggers (a fresh rumor after a loss, a targeted rumor, or a journal replacement when every copy is carried), and replacements are limited to one per player per carrier interval. That removes the tracker loop, halves the staleness state machine, and gives the property test a simple rule to check: no player gets more than one carrier sector per 30 s before minute 28.
cheap_experiment: Before building the full module, write one scripted test against a stub with the draft staleness rule. All three Moon copies are carried. The thief sails from North-West Reach through Central Waters into South-East over 90 s (1,800 ticks), and the victim holds a Moon carrier-sighting rumor. Count the messages the victim gets and the ticks they arrive on. More than one sighting per 30 s, or a stale mark on the tick of a live sector crossing, means the generic staleness rule is a tracker and the carrier-sighting rule has to change. The same half-hour also confirms 20·60·20 = 24,000 > 20,000, which settles how the property config reaches the reveals.
